mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with declines in FEDFUNDS, or if the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns despite rising unemployment, or if the mechanism fails to predict negative returns in 70% of triggered cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates reduced demand in the housing market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as related industries experience slowdowns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns following a 5% decline in HOUST, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) combined with rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are squeezed.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns during periods of slowing GDP growth and rising inflation, or if the mechanism fails to predict negative returns in 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates tighter monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and consumer spending slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or if the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are impacted.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns during periods of declining industrial production, or if the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in payroll employment (PAYEMS) during a late-cycle expansion indicates impending economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as businesses reduce hiring and investment.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns during periods of slowing payroll growth in late-cycle expansions, or if the mechanism fails to predict negative returns in 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer and business confidence declines.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns during periods of slowing GDP growth and rising unemployment, or if the Rank IC falls below 0.03.
